conventions.k: 1k tokens = 1,024 tokens in context lengths (2k = 2,048 ... 128k = 131,072); 'per 1,000 tokens' is stated where decimal is meant.

tp_sharding.note: Each GPU holds the K and V of exactly 1 KV head (shared by its 12 query heads) for every token and every layer. Attention needs no cross-GPU traffic; the o_proj all-reduce combines the heads.

consequences.max_batch: The KV pool, not compute, caps the batch at long context: one 8-GPU node of M-dense (BF16 weights, BF16 KV) holds 101 sequences at 8,192 tokens but 6 at 131,072 tokens.
consequences.admission_policy: One 131,072-token sequence takes 11.2% of the KV pool in the engine-default case (fp8_weights_bf16_kv). Admission must check free blocks, or the engine preempts running sequences when an allocation fails.
consequences.routing: KV use per request scales with context: a 131,072-token request uses 64× the blocks of a 2,048-token one. Routing by request count ignores this; KV-aware routing (free blocks, cached prefix) does not.
consequences.gpu_count: GPUs for N concurrent 8k sequences = ceil(N / sequences per node) × 8: 80 H100 with BF16 weights and KV, 32 with FP8 weights and KV.
consequences.fp8_kv_effect: FP8 KV halves KV bytes per token; with FP8 weights it raises 8k sequences per node from 142 to 285.
consequences.k3_state_bound: For K3 on a DEP16 rank, FP8 MLA raises 2,048-token sequences per rank from 100 to 106 only: short requests are bound by the fixed KDA state, not by KV.
